chunks: Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

He said: I asked him about a man who sleeps through the morning prayer until the sun rises: should he pray when he wakes up, or should he wait until the sun has spread? He said: He should pray when he wakes up. I said: Should he perform the witr, or pray two rak'ahs? He said: Rather, he should begin with the obligatory prayer.

key_terms.الْغَدَاةِ: the morning prayer time, referring here to salat al-fajr
key_terms.تَبْزُغَ: to rise, referring to the sun's rising

ai.seo_question: If someone sleeps through the morning prayer until sunrise, should he pray immediately upon waking or wait?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the ruling for one who misses the morning prayer by sleeping until sunrise. When he wakes, he should perform the missed obligatory prayer immediately and not delay it for the sun to rise further, nor begin with supererogatory prayer before the fard prayer.
